title: 1971 AHSME Problem 5
statement: Points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(Q,\) \(D,\) and \(C\) lie on the circle shown, and the measures of arcs \(BQ\) and \(QD\) are \(42^\circ\) and \(38^\circ,\) respectively. The sum of the measures of angles \(P\) and \(Q\) is:

solutions.text:
Let \(m\widehat{AC}=u.\) The external-secant formula gives \[ m\angle P=\frac12\left(m\widehat{BD}-u\right), \] while the inscribed-angle theorem gives \(m\angle Q=\frac{u}{2}.\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} m\angle P+m\angle Q &=\frac12m\widehat{BD}\\ &=\frac12(42^\circ+38^\circ)\\ &=40^\circ. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use the external-secant formula for angle \(P\)
Adding angle \(Q\) cancels the unknown intercepted arc
